# PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS] Contents of this Part

## I GENERAL RULES ABOUT DETAILED ASSESSMENT

## Time when detailed assessment may be carried out

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > Time when detailed assessment may be carried out] 47.1 The general rule is that the costs of any proceedings or any part of the proceedings are not to be assessed by the detailed procedure until the conclusion of the proceedings, but the court may order them to be assessed immediately. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > Time when detailed assessment may be carried out] (Practice Direction 47 gives further guidance about when proceedings are concluded for the purpose of this rule.)

## No stay of detailed assessment where there is an appeal

## 47.2 Detailed assessment is not stayed pending an appeal unless the court so orders. ## Powers of an authorised court officer

## 47.3

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.3] (1) An authorised court officer has all the powers of the court when making a detailed assessment, except –

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.3] (a) power to make a wasted costs order as defined in rule 46.8;

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.3] (b) power to make an order under –

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.3] (i) rule 44.11 (powers in relation to misconduct);

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.3] (ii) rules 47.8 (sanction for delay in commencing detailed assessment proceedings) and 47.14.(3) and (4) (sanction for delay in requesting a detailed assessment hearing);

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.3] (iii) paragraph (2) (objection to detailed assessment by authorised court officer); and

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.3] (c) power to make a detailed assessment of costs payable to a solicitor by that solicitor’s client, unless the costs are being assessed under rule 46.4 (costs where money is payable to a child or protected party). [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.3] (2) Where a party objects to the detailed assessment of costs being made by an authorised court officer, the court may order it to be made by a costs judge or a district judge. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.3] (Practice Direction 47 sets out the relevant procedure.)

## Venue for detailed assessment proceedings

## 47.4

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.4] (1) All applications and requests in detailed assessment proceedings must be made to or filed at the appropriate office. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.4] (Practice Direction 47 sets out the meaning of ‘appropriate office’ in any particular case)

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.4] (2) The court may direct that the appropriate office is to be the Costs Office. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.4] (3) In the County Court, a court may direct that another County Court hearing centre is to be the appropriate office. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.4] (4) A direction under paragraph (3) may be made without proceedings being transferred to that court. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.4] (Rule 30.2 makes provision for the transfer within the County Court of proceedings for detailed assessment of costs.)

## II COSTS PAYABLE BY ONE PARTY TO ANOTHER – COMMENCEMENT OF DETAILED ASSESSMENT PROCEEDINGS

## Application of this Section

## 47.5 This Section of Part 47 applies where a cost officer is to make a detailed assessment of –

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.5 This Section of Part 47 applies where a cost officer is to make a detailed assessment of –] (a) costs which are payable by one party to another; or

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.5 This Section of Part 47 applies where a cost officer is to make a detailed assessment of –] (b) the sum which is payable by one party to the prescribed charity pursuant to an order under section 194(3) of the 2007 Act. ## Commencement of detailed assessment proceedings

## 47.6

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.6] (1) Detailed assessment proceedings are commenced by the receiving party serving on the paying party –

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.6] (a) notice of commencement in the relevant practice form;

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.6] (b) a copy or copies of the bill of costs, as required by Practice Direction 47; and (c) if required by Practice Direction 47,

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.6] (Rule 47.7 sets out the period for commencing detailed assessment proceedings.)

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.6] (2) The receiving party must also serve a copy of the notice of commencement, the bill and, if required by Practice Direction 47, the breakdown on any other relevant persons specified in Practice Direction 47. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.6] (3) A person on whom a copy of the notice of commencement is served under paragraph (2) is a party to the detailed assessment proceedings (in addition to the paying party and the receiving party). [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.6] (Practice Direction 47 deals with –

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.6] other documents which the party must file when requesting detailed assessment;

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.6] the court’s powers where it considers that a hearing may be necessary;

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.6] the form of a bill; and

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.6] the length of notice which will be given if a hearing date is fixed.)

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.6] (Paragraphs 7B.2 to 7B.7 of the Practice Direction – Civil Recovery Proceedings contain provisions about detailed assessment of costs in relation to civil recovery orders.)

## Period for commencing detailed assessment proceedings

## 47.7 The following table shows the period for commencing detailed assessment proceedings. ## Sanction for delay in commencing detailed assessment proceedings

## 47.8

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.8] (1) Where the receiving party fails to commence detailed assessment proceedings within the period specified –

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.8] (a) in rule 47.7; or

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.8] (b) by any direction of the court,

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.8] the paying party may apply for an order requiring the receiving party to commence detailed assessment proceedings within such time as the court may specify. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.8] (2) On an application under paragraph (1), the court may direct that, unless the receiving party commences detailed assessment proceedings within the time specified by the court, all or part of the costs to which the receiving party would otherwise be entitled will be disallowed. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.8] (3) If –

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.8] (a) the paying party has not made an application in accordance with paragraph (1); and

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.8] (b) the receiving party commences the proceedings later than the period specified in rule 47.7,

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.8] the court may disallow all or part of the interest otherwise payable to the receiving party under –

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.8] (i) section 17 of the Judgments Act 1838 1 ; or

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.8] (ii) section 74 of the County Courts Act 1984 2 ,

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.8] but will not impose any other sanction except in accordance with rule 44.11 (powers in relation to misconduct). [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.8] (4) Where the costs to be assessed in a detailed assessment are payable out of the Community Legal Service Fund, this rule applies as if the receiving party were the solicitor to whom the costs are payable and the paying party were the Legal Services Commission. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.8] (5) Where the costs to be assessed in a detailed assessment are payable by the Lord Chancellor under Part 1 of the Legal Aid, Sentencing and Punishment of Offenders Act 2012, this rule applies as if the receiving party were the solicitor to whom the costs are payable and the paying party were the Lord Chancellor. ## Points of dispute and consequence of not serving

## 47.9

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.9] (1) The paying party and any other party to the detailed assessment proceedings may dispute any item in the bill of costs by serving points of dispute on –

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.9] (a) the receiving party; and

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.9] (b) every other party to the detailed assessment proceedings. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.9] (2) The period for serving points of dispute is 21 days after the date of service of the notice of commencement. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.9] (3) If a party serves points of dispute after the period set out in paragraph (2), that party may not be heard further in the detailed assessment proceedings unless the court gives permission. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.9] (Practice Direction 47 sets out requirements about the form of points of dispute.)

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.9] (4) The receiving party may file a request for a default costs certificate if –

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.9] (a) the period set out in paragraph (2) for serving points of dispute has expired; and

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.9] (b) the receiving party has not been served with any points of dispute. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.9] (5) If any party (including the paying party) serves points of dispute before the issue of a default costs certificate the court may not issue the default costs certificate. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.9] (Section IV of this Part sets out the procedure to be followed after points of dispute have been served.)

## Procedure where costs are agreed

## 47.10

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.10] (1) If the paying party and the receiving party agree the amount of costs, either party may apply for a costs certificate (either interim or final) in the amount agreed. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.10] (Rule 47.16 and rule 47.17 contain further provisions about interim and final costs certificates respectively)

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.10] (2) An application for a certificate under paragraph (1) must be made to the court which would be the venue for detailed assessment proceedings under rule 47.4. ## III COSTS PAYABLE BY ONE PARTY TO ANOTHER – DEFAULT PROVISIONS

## Default costs certificate

## 47.11

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.11] (1) Where the receiving party is permitted by rule 47.9 to obtain a default costs certificate, that party does so by filing a request in the relevant practice form. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.11] ( Practice Direction 47 deals with the procedure by which the receiving party may obtain a default costs certificate.)

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.11] (2) A default costs certificate will include an order to pay the costs to which it relates. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.11] (3) Where a receiving party obtains a default costs certificate, the costs payable to that party for the commencement of detailed assessment proceedings will be the sum set out in Practice Direction 47. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.11] (4) A receiving party who obtains a default costs certificate in detailed assessment proceedings pursuant to an order under section 194(3) of the 2007 Act must send a copy of the default costs certificate to the prescribed charity. ## Setting aside a default costs certificate

## 47.12

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.12] (1) The court will set aside a default costs certificate if the receiving party was not entitled to it. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.12] (2) In any other case, the court may set aside or vary a default costs certificate if it appears to the court that there is some good reason why the detailed assessment proceedings should continue. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.12] (Practice Direction 47 contains further details about the procedure for setting aside a default costs certificate and the matters which the court must take into account)

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.12] (3) Where the court sets aside or varies a default costs certificate in detailed assessment proceedings pursuant to an order under section 194(3) of the Legal Services Act 2007, the receiving party must send a copy of the order setting aside or varying the default costs certificate to the prescribed charity. ## IV COSTS PAYABLE BY ONE PARTY TO ANOTHER – PROCEDURE WHERE POINTS OF DISPUTE ARE SERVED

## Optional Reply

## 47.13

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.13] (1) Where any party to the detailed assessment proceedings serves points of dispute, the receiving party may serve a reply on the other parties to the assessment proceedings. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.13] (2) The receiving party may do so within 21 days after being served with the points of dispute to which the reply relates. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.13] (Practice Direction 47 sets out the meaning of ‘reply’.)

## Detailed assessment hearing

## 47.14

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.14] (1) Where points of dispute are served in accordance with this Part, the receiving party must file a request for a detailed assessment hearing within 3 months of the expiry of the period for commencing detailed assessment proceedings as specified –

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.14] (a) in rule 47.7; or

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.14] (b) by any direction of the court. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.14] (2) Where the receiving party fails to file a request in accordance with paragraph (1), the paying party may apply for an order requiring the receiving party to file the request within such time as the court may specify. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.14] (3) On an application under paragraph (2), the court may direct that, unless the receiving party requests a detailed assessment hearing within the time specified by the court, all or part of the costs to which the receiving party would otherwise be entitled will be disallowed. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.14] (4) If –

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.14] (a) the paying party has not made an application in accordance with paragraph (2); and

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.14] (b) the receiving party files a request for a detailed assessment hearing later than the period specified in paragraph (1),

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.14] the court may disallow all or part of the interest otherwise payable to the receiving party under –

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.14] (i) section 17 of the Judgments Act 1838; or

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.14] (ii) section 74 of the County Courts Act 1984,

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.14] but will not impose any other sanction except in accordance with rule 44.11 (powers in relation to misconduct). [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.14] (5) No party other than –

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.14] (a) the receiving party;

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.14] (b) the paying party; and

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.14] (c) any party who has served points of dispute under rule 47.9,

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.14] may be heard at the detailed assessment hearing unless the court gives permission. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.14] (6) Only items specified in the points of dispute may be raised at the hearing, unless the court gives permission. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.14] (7) If an assessment is carried out at more than one hearing, then for the purposes of rule 52.12 time for appealing shall not start to run until the conclusion of the final hearing, unless the court orders otherwise. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.14] (Practice Direction 47 specifies other documents which must be filed with the request for hearing and the length of notice which the court will give when it fixes a hearing date.)

## Provisional Assessment

## 47.15

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.15] (1) This rule applies to any detailed assessment proceedings commenced in the High Court or the County Court on or after 1 April 2013 in which the costs claimed are the amount set out in paragraph 14.1 of the practice direction supplementing this Part, or less. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.15] (2) In proceedings to which this rule applies, the parties must comply with the procedure set out in Part 47 as modified by paragraph 14 Practice Direction 47. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.15] (3) The court will undertake a provisional assessment of the receiving party’s costs on receipt of Form N258 and the relevant supporting documents specified in Practice Direction 47. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.15] (4) The provisional assessment will be based on the information contained in the bill and supporting papers and the contentions set out in Precedent G (the points of dispute and any reply). [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.15] (5) In proceedings which do not go beyond provisional assessment, the maximum amount the court will award to any party as costs of the assessment (other than the costs of drafting the bill of costs) is £1,500 together with any VAT thereon and any court fees paid by that party. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.15] (6) The court may at any time decide that the matter is unsuitable for a provisional assessment and may give directions for the matter to be listed for hearing. The matter will then proceed under rule 47.14 without modification. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.15] (7) When a provisional assessment has been carried out, the court will send a copy of the bill, as provisionally assessed, to each party with a notice stating that any party who wishes to challenge any aspect of the provisional assessment must, within 21 days of the receipt of the notice, file and serve on all other parties a written request for an oral hearing. If no such request is filed and served within that period, the provisional assessment shall be binding upon the parties, save in exceptional circumstances. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.15] (8) The written request referred to in paragraph (7) must –

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.15] (a) identify the item or items in the court’s provisional assessment which are sought to be reviewed at the hearing; and

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.15] (b) provide a time estimate for the hearing. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.15] (9) The court then will fix a date for the hearing and give at least 14 days’ notice of the time and place of the hearing to all parties. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.15] (10) Any party which has requested an oral hearing, will pay the costs of and incidental to that hearing unless –

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.15] (a) it achieves an adjustment in its own favour by 20% or more of the sum provisionally assessed; or

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.15] (b) the court otherwise orders. ## V INTERIM COSTS CERTIFICATE AND FINAL COSTS CERTIFICATE

## Power to issue an interim certificate

## 47.16

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.16] (1) The court may at any time after the receiving party has filed a request for a detailed assessment hearing –

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.16] (a) issue an interim costs certificate for such sum as it considers appropriate; or

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.16] (b) amend or cancel an interim certificate. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.16] (2) An interim certificate will include an order to pay the costs to which it relates, unless the court orders otherwise. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.16] (3) The court may order the costs certified in an interim certificate to be paid into court. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.16] (4) Where the court –

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.16] (a) issues an interim costs certificate; or

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.16] (b) amends or cancels an interim certificate,

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.16] in detailed assessment proceedings pursuant to an order under section 194(3) of the 2007 Act, the receiving party must send a copy of the interim costs certificate or the order amending or cancelling the interim costs certificate to the prescribed charity. ## Final costs certificate

## 47.17

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.17] (1) In this rule a ‘completed bill’ means a bill calculated to show the amount due following the detailed assessment of the costs. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.17] (2) The period for filing the completed bill is 14 days after the end of the detailed assessment hearing. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.17] (3) When a completed bill is filed the court will issue a final costs certificate and serve it on the parties to the detailed assessment proceedings. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.17] (4) Paragraph (3) is subject to any order made by the court that a certificate is not to be issued until other costs have been paid. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.17] (5) A final costs certificate will include an order to pay the costs to which it relates, unless the court orders otherwise. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.17] (Practice Direction 47 deals with the form of a final costs certificate.)

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.17] (6) Where the court issues a final costs certificate in detailed assessment proceedings pursuant to an order under section 194(3) of the 2007 Act, the receiving party must send a copy of the final costs certificate to the prescribed charity. ## 47.18

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.18] (1) Where the court is to assess costs of a LSC funded client, an assisted person or a person to whom legal aid is provided which are payable out of the Community Legal Services Fund or by the Lord Chancellor under Part 1 of the Legal Aid, Sentencing and Punishment of Offenders Act 2012, that person’s solicitor may commence detailed assessment proceedings by filing a request in the relevant practice form. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.18] (2) A request under paragraph (1) must be filed within 3 months after the date when the right to detailed assessment arose. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.18] (3) The solicitor must also serve a copy of the request for detailed assessment on the LSC funded client, the assisted person or the person to whom legal aid is provided, if notice of that person’s interest has been given to the court in accordance with community legal service or legal aid regulations. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.18] (4) Where the solicitor has certified that the LSC funded client or that person wishes to attend an assessment hearing, the court will, on receipt of the request for assessment, fix a date for the assessment hearing. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.18] (5) Where paragraph (3) does not apply, the court will, on receipt of the request for assessment provisionally assess the costs without the attendance of the solicitor, unless it considers that a hearing is necessary. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.18] (6) After the court has provisionally assessed the bill, it will return the bill to the solicitor. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.18] (7) The court will fix a date for an assessment hearing if the solicitor informs the court, within 14 days after receiving the provisionally assessed bill, that the solicitor wants the court to hold such a hearing. ## 47.19

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.19] (1) Where the court is to assess costs which are payable out of a fund other than the Community Legal Service Fund, the receiving party may commence detailed assessment proceedings by filing a request in the relevant practice form. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.19] (2) A request under paragraph (1) must be filed within 3 months after the date when the right to detailed assessment arose. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.19] (3) The court may direct that the party seeking assessment serve a copy of the request on any person who has a financial interest in the outcome of the assessment. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.19] (4) The court will, on receipt of the request for assessment, provisionally assess the costs without the attendance of the receiving party, unless the court considers that a hearing is necessary. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.19] (5) After the court has provisionally assessed the bill, it will return the bill to the receiving party. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.19] (6) The court will fix a date for an assessment hearing if the receiving party informs the court, within 14 days after receiving the provisionally assessed bill, that the receiving party wants the court to hold such a hearing. ## VII COSTS OF DETAILED ASSESSMENT PROCEEDINGS

## Liability for costs of detailed assessment proceedings

## 47.20

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.20] (1) The receiving party is entitled to the costs of the detailed assessment proceedings except where –

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.20] (a) the provisions of any Act, any of these Rules or any relevant practice direction provide otherwise; or

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.20] (b) the court makes some other order in relation to all or part of the costs of the detailed assessment proceedings. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.20] (2) Paragraph (1) does not apply where the receiving party has pro bono representation in the detailed assessment proceedings but that party may apply for an order in respect of that representation under section 194(3) of the 2007 Act.
